newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico key Cetes rate continues slide, others rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexico key Cetes rate continues slide, others rise.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate fell for the third straight week at the primary auction on Monday, following sliding rates in the secondary money market, analysts said.
But fear of what could happen later in the year helped drive rates higher on the longer-term paper, steepening the yield curve, they said.
"The drop in the short-term paper was expected and follows what we saw in the secondary money market...," said Ricardo Vazquez, an analyst with Banco Union.
The rate on the one-month paper fell 52 basis points to 19.71 percent at Banco de Mexico's auction.
Overnight Cetes rates shrugged off a weak peso and fell 140 basis points to close at 18.0 percent in the secondary market on Monday.
A survey of nine money market dealers earlier in the day found expectations of a decline of 23 basis points on the one-month paper and rising longer-term rates.
But investors showed more caution on the longer end of the yield curve.
The rate on the 92-day paper rose 15 basis points to 22.08 percent, while 183-day paper saw a rise of 72 basis points to 23.18 percent.
One-year paper yielded 24.35 percent compared with 23.72 percent last week.
"Investors are cautious because of the elections, uncertainty over U.S. interest rates and other events," said Interacciones economist Alonso Cervera.
Some investors have been worried that key mid-term elections in Mexico in July could cause some political and financial turmoil.
Analysts said good demand for the longer-term paper showed that investors were still placing bids despite being cautious.
Overall auction demand fell from the extremely strong 19.02 billion seen at the auction last week but remained at a respectable 13.99 billion pesos this week.
Demand was heaviest for the 92-day and 183-day paper, which had bid-to-cover ratios of 5.81 and 5.17, respectively.
With declining inflationary pressures, real returns remain high on the shorter-term Cetes, returning about 7.0 percent in peso terms, analysts said.
J.P. Morgan said in a report that it sees inflation weak in Mexico for most part for the rest of the year.

"From here on and for most of the rest of 1997, until the year-end seasonal period starts again, Morgan expects inflation to trend in a range close to 0.5 percent for biweekly figures and 1.1 percent for monthly figures," the company said in a report released on Monday.
The auction was held one day earlier than normal to allow for settlement before the May Day holiday in Mexico on Thursday.
